answer: One concrete mechanism: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because copper only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. In practice wharf is enforced by the ledger itself: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any zenith approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
